The synthetic control estimate of the ATT of Proposition 99 is about -41.71 packs per capita, so the proposition reduced cigarette sales.

I built the synthetic California as a weighted average of the other states' `cigsale` series. The weights were non-negative and summed to 1, and I chose them to match California's sales over 1970–1988. The ATT is the average gap between actual California sales and this synthetic California over the post-treatment years, 1989–2000. I took 1988 as the last pre-treatment year and did not check that against the `after_treatment` column in the data.

ANSWER: -41.71
